Evidence index

Every engineering claim this site makes in public, with the status of its verification, somewhere you can go and check it, and the limitation that goes with it.

Every capability shown here is tied to inspectable evidence and an explicit verification level.

This platform is my own system, which I build and operate myself. It is not an employer’s product, and the traffic on it is mine.

How verification works

Each claim on this page is generated from a registry, not written here by hand. A build check refuses the registry if a claim has no evidence, if a destination does not resolve, or if a status is higher than the verification actually recorded for that capability — so a claim cannot quietly outgrow its evidence, and the page cannot drift from the registry, because regenerating it is enforced by a test.

What that check deliberately does not do is read a claim and decide whether it is true. A script decides whether a claim has evidence, a destination and a stated limitation. A person decides whether it is true. Mechanising the second would read as stronger and would be worse: a confident false pass from a truth-checker is more dangerous than no truth-checker at all.

The four verification levels are defined below, and every capability carries its limitation in the open rather than behind this disclosure.

How to read a status

  • LiveRunning right now and independently inspectable -- the visitor can open it.
  • TestedDemonstrated by deterministic tests or recorded evidence, even where the visitor cannot execute it themselves.
  • DocumentedSupported by source, history or a case study, but not publicly runnable.
  • Experimental / pausedResearch or experimental work, stated with its limitations, not a working product.

Where to start

Recruiter or HR

Who is this, what role, why different, and where is the proof?

  1. Start with the three proof points on the home page.
  2. Open one live thing — the Workbench, or the running Java application.
  3. Read the limitation under any claim that matters to you.

AI / agentic hiring manager

Is the agent work real -- authority boundaries, durability, evaluation, security?

  1. The write boundary: an agent with no code path to approve itself.
  2. The durable workflow case study, including where the crash drill stops.
  3. Retrieval with a measured evaluation gate, and the model kill switch.
  4. The paused experiment — what it falsified, and why it was stopped.

Backend or architecture interviewer

Is there a real Java/Spring system under this, with real tests and real architecture reasoning?

  1. Open the running Java/Spring application.
  2. The schema migrations and the real-PostgreSQL CI run.
  3. The multi-service decomposition and its real-topology test tier.
  4. The durable workflow's Postgres checkpointing.

The strongest evidence

An AI agent that cannot approve its own writes

Live

A change proposed by the model is applied only after a person approves it, and the approval is tied to the exact file and content that was approved. The approve step is not something the model can call.

Limitation: Covers writes through this platform only; not a general policy engine.

View evidence
Evidence
Approval is bound to sha256(path, content) and re-checked at apply time. Tests prove that a content substitution and a path substitution after approval are each rejected, and that approve and reject are absent from the tool schemas by exact set membership.
Limitation in full
The boundary governs writes made through this platform's own tools, scoped to three path prefixes and two file extensions. It is not a general-purpose policy engine, and it does not govern anything changed outside the platform.
In the source
agent/write_tools.py, agent/execution_tools.py, agent/build_tools.py
Go and check it
How the boundary works → The tests that prove it → Watch it run →

Registry id: hitl-hash-bound-write-boundary

A workflow that survives a crash

Live

Long-running work saves its progress as it goes, so it can pause for a human decision and continue after a restart without repeating anything it already did.

Limitation: Mid-pipeline crash proven locally; in production only a restart while awaiting approval.

View evidence
Evidence
Crash drill 22 of 22 in one run: a real child process killed after the git commit and before the checkpoint, resumed by a fresh process with exactly one commit and compile, test and verify completed. A corrupt checkpoint row is reported as CORRUPT rather than resumed.
Limitation in full
The crash drill's process kills were performed locally. In production what has been demonstrated is a restart while the workflow was waiting for approval -- not a kill in the middle of the pipeline, because the pipeline completes in about five seconds and has no pause hook there.
In the source
agent/durable_workflow.py, agent/workflow_checkpointer.py, agent/workflow_drill.py, agent/test_durable_workflow.py
Go and check it
Read the case study → The workflow and its checkpointer → The crash drill →

Retrieval that is measured, not assumed

Tested

Search quality is scored against a hand-labelled set of questions and expected answers, and the build fails if the scores drop below the recorded thresholds. The same read-only repository tools are also exposed over the Model Context Protocol so other AI clients can use them.

Limitation: Local index over small corpora, no managed vector DB, no hybrid search or reranking.

View evidence
Evidence
Measured baseline recall@3 0.833, recall@5 0.917, MRR 0.826, routing accuracy 1.0, security-case accuracy 1.0. The corpus expansion from 10 to 28 files was a disclosed precision/coverage trade-off, not a silent one.
Limitation in full
Retrieval is a local JSON index with a numpy cosine scan over small corpora, not a managed vector database, and there is no hybrid search or reranking. The MCP server runs locally rather than as a hosted service.
In the source
agent/rag_index.py, agent/mcp_server.py, agent/backend_rag_index.py, agent/eval_runner.py
Go and check it
Ask the codebase yourself → The evaluation gate → The MCP server →

Registry id: rag-mcp-embeddings

One model boundary, with a kill switch

Live

Every call to a language model goes through one place, which checks what the call is for and can be switched off entirely. A test fails the build if any code tries to bypass it.

Limitation: Single provider; no multi-provider routing or failover.

View evidence
Evidence
An enforcement test fails the build on any direct SDK import outside the gateway -- it caught the first version of the Standing Interview importing the SDK directly. A denial is reported as its own state rather than returned as an empty answer.
Limitation in full
It is a single-provider boundary. Multi-provider routing and failover are not implemented, and the purpose allowlist is a fixed list rather than a policy language.
In the source
agent/reasoning_gateway.py, agent/test_reasoning_gateway.py, agent/test_reasoning_gateway_enforcement.py

Every meaningful step and every model call is written to a durable log, including real token counts. If the log's database is unreachable the events are held locally and sent later rather than lost.

An experiment that failed its own test, and was stopped

Experimental / paused

A multi-model cross-review engine was built to a decision rule fixed in advance, measured against frozen ground truth, and then paused when the evidence failed that rule. The product thesis is unproven. The strongest finding is about measurement rather than the product: every recent headline turned out to be produced by a defect in the evaluation system, in both directions.

Limitation: PAUSED and the product thesis is UNPROVEN: zero genuine corrections demonstrated. Not an accuracy product.

View evidence
Evidence
20 of 20 pre-registered cases run exactly once, 0 paid API calls, evidence integrity 16 of 16, mutation gate 19 killed and 0 survived, and an offline self-replay that reproduces the verdict with 0 differences and 0 model calls. 13 defects were found in the final sprint alone -- nine in the scorer, two in identity and routing that would have published a false agreement. The mechanical verdict and the Owner's adjudication of the same frozen evidence differed, and both are preserved rather than reconciled.
Limitation in full
PAUSED, and the product thesis is UNPROVEN. It demonstrated zero genuine false-to-true corrections and zero genuine baseline false claims, so it must not be read as an accuracy product, as evidence that multiple models improve correctness, or as a partial success. It is evidence of experiment design and engineering judgement, nothing more.
In the source
docs/DEEP_CONSENSUS_CASE_STUDY.md, docs/DEEP_CONSENSUS_FINAL_CLOSURE_2026-10-02.md, docs/evidence/deep-consensus-sprint6/evidence-integrity-manifest.json, docs/evidence/deep-consensus-sprint6/sprint6-selfreplay-report.json
Go and check it

Also verifiable

The implementer does not certify its own work

Tested

A structurally separate evaluator re-verifies an AI-generated change against real evidence, and the implementer never gets the last word on whether its own change succeeded.

Limitation: Same-model review is an independent evidence path, not an independent mind; shared blind spots remain.

View evidence
Evidence
A deliberately seeded defect (a capitalisation mismatch) was independently caught with byte-exact evidence.
Limitation in full
A second instance of the same model is an independent evidence path, not an independent mind. It reliably catches unverified claims, skipped gates and absent observable effects; it shares blind spots with the implementer on subtle logic errors, and that residual risk is unsolved rather than managed.
In the source
.claude/agents/qa-evaluator.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE_V2_EVALUATION_PLAN.md
Go and check it

AI-assisted delivery that is actually estimated

Tested

Every task is sized with a numeric range and a confidence before work starts; each sprint ends in a retrospective comparing estimate to actual, with every gap outside tolerance diagnosed as either a wrong estimate or an implementation problem, and the verdict computed by a script rather than judged.

Limitation: The tolerance verdict is computed; the sizing gate itself is still applied by hand.

View evidence
Evidence
Multiple sprints of recorded sizes, actuals and ratios verified against real git commit timestamps, including one retrospective whose own conclusion was corrected by an independent adversarial review.
Limitation in full
The tolerance verdict is computed, but the sizing gate itself is not mechanised -- it is applied by hand, and that is recorded as an open item rather than described as automated.

agent/backlog.py, agent/verify_tracking_updated.py, agent/check_id_available.py
